Prices would crash hard initially (markets tend to overreact on this kind of thing) and then start rising again as demand catches up with the new supply. The price per unit is ultimately set by the production cost per unit, though, so if the production cost falls dramatically (which is what they're talking about here) then the price per unit will follow relatively soon.

The amusing part is that the crash in prices could well happen while the asteroid's still on its way back to Earth. It would take at least months if not years for a full round trip. It's not like you can keep something that big a secret, not when anyone with a telescope can see you on your way back with an asteroid in tow. You'd probably see a massive price spike in the shares of the company bringing the asteroid back before it arrives at least, but prices in the rare materials being brought back crash shortly thereafter. This'd be a lot different to galleons coming back from the New World loaded up with spices and other goodies; technology and the sheer size of the haul changes how the market would behave I'd have thought.
